key_insight: Single-crystal Ti-15Mo shows inverted elastic anisotropy, with near-⟨111⟩ orientations softest in modulus and yield onset, while simple CRSS/Schmid-factor models fail to reproduce the yield response.
engineering_relevance: Texture-sensitive constitutive models for Ti-15Mo should distinguish elastic stiffness, yield onset, and hardness rather than assume a shared orientation dependence.
method: Correlate EBSD-measured orientation with nanoindentation across five crystallographic directions.
Measure indentation modulus, hardness, yield onset, and strain-rate sensitivity.
Use strain-rate jumps to estimate activation volumes and assess deformation mechanisms.
evidence_signal: Across the tested orientations, modulus varied by ~10%, yield onset by 41%, and hardness by 6.6%; activation volumes of 18–31b³ were consistent with kink-pair-controlled plasticity.
watch_item: Retained athermal ω and reversible ω→β transformation are proposed contributors to the inverted anisotropy, not directly established mechanisms in the abstract.
paper_title: Orientation-Resolved Nanoindentation of Single Crystal Ti-15Mo: Inverted Elastic Anisotropy and Yield-Onset Behavior Beyond Simple CRSS Predictions
